title: The History of the Souls Games | Demon's Souls to Elden Ring | Gaming History
description: The full history of FromSoftware's Souls games: Demon's Souls, Dark Souls, Bloodborne, Sekiro, Elden Ring, Shadow of the Erdtree and Nightreign, with Hidetaka Miyazaki and the biggest sales milestones.

sections.heading: Prepare to die
sections.script: A lonely knight, a bonfire and a boss that ends your run in seconds. The Souls games from FromSoftware have become some of the most respected and most talked about games of the last fifteen years. They taught a generation of players that dying is part of learning, and they turned a niche Japanese role playing game into a worldwide phenomenon. In this video we walk through the history of the Souls series: from Demon's Souls in two thousand nine, through Dark Souls, Bloodborne and Sekiro, to Elden Ring, which won Game of the Year in twenty twenty two, and the newest spin offs. We will look at the director behind it all, Hidetaka Miyazaki, and at the sales milestones that surprised even the publisher. Let's light the bonfire.

sections.heading: Demon's Souls
sections.script: Our story begins in two thousand nine with Demon's Souls on the PlayStation 3. FromSoftware was known for niche role playing games, and this project was not going well. Hidetaka Miyazaki took over its development when it stalled, and he helped shape it into the dark, difficult adventure we know. The game had a tough start in sales, but word of mouth was strong. After a few months it turned around, and overseas distribution began. Demon's Souls introduced the ideas that define the whole genre: harsh enemies, careful combat, a world that does not explain itself, and the feeling of victory after a long struggle. Years later, in June of twenty twenty, Sony revealed a remake from Bluepoint Games for the PlayStation 5, proof of how loved the original had become.

sections.heading: Dark Souls arrives
sections.script: Two years later, Miyazaki directed a spiritual successor called Dark Souls. It was released in Japan on September twenty second, twenty eleven, for PlayStation 3 and Xbox 360, with the worldwide release following in October. It built on the ideas of Demon's Souls and trusted players to learn from their mistakes. It was not an instant blockbuster, but it grew into a cult hit and is now often listed among the greatest games of all time. Fans spent hundreds of hours in it, and the series name became shorthand for a hard but fair challenge. A remastered version followed in May of twenty eighteen, bringing the first game to a new audience on modern hardware and giving newcomers an easy way to see where the series truly began.

sections.heading: Dark Souls Two and a new job for Miyazaki
sections.script: Dark Souls Two arrived in twenty fourteen, with Miyazaki supervising but not directing. In the same year, Miyazaki was promoted to president of FromSoftware, which gave him even more influence over the studio. Meanwhile he was working on something different, a project that would show the studio could do much more than castles and knights. Bloodborne, an exclusive for PlayStation 4, launched on March twenty fourth, twenty fifteen, and moved away from the medieval knights of Dark Souls to a new setting and a different style. It became a cult favorite, and Miyazaki himself has been described as having a special fondness for it. Fans have asked for a sequel ever since, and the debate about it is one of the longest running topics in gaming.

sections.heading: Dark Souls Three
sections.script: In two thousand sixteen came Dark Souls Three, directed by Miyazaki and widely seen as the grand finale of the trilogy. Miyazaki had said in twenty fifteen that it would likely be the last in the series. It also became the biggest hit of the series. Bandai Namco announced that Dark Souls Three had passed ten million copies sold worldwide, more than four years after release. At that time the whole Dark Souls series had reached about twenty seven million copies, and Dark Souls Three accounted for over a third of them. It had sold about three million copies in its first month alone, and in June of twenty nineteen FromSoftware had reported a series total of twenty five million. Those numbers show how far the idea had traveled since the quiet start of Demon's Souls. For many fans it is the perfect starting point for the series, with a strong mix of difficulty, atmosphere and some of the best boss fights in the genre.

sections.heading: Sekiro takes the crown
sections.script: In March of twenty nineteen, FromSoftware surprised everyone with Sekiro: Shadows Die Twice, published by Activision. It was another Miyazaki directed adventure, this time starring a shinobi, and it was a very different game from Dark Souls. Many players found it tough, but critics loved it. At The Game Awards two thousand nineteen, Sekiro won Game of the Year, beating Control, Death Stranding, Resident Evil Two, Super Smash Bros. Ultimate and The Outer Worlds. It also won the award for Best Action and Adventure Game, an impressive double for a studio best known for one style of game. It proved that FromSoftware could succeed far beyond its Souls formula.

sections.heading: Elden Ring changes everything
sections.script: Then came the big one. Elden Ring launched on February twenty fifth, twenty twenty two, for PlayStation 4, PlayStation 5, Xbox One, Xbox Series X and S, and PC. It was directed by Miyazaki, with the world and mythology created together with George R. R. Martin, the author of A Song of Ice and Fire. The big new idea was a huge open world that you could explore freely, with the help of your spirit steed Torrent. It won Game of the Year at The Game Awards two thousand twenty two. Sales were enormous. FromSoftware and Bandai Namco reported more than twenty million units shipped by February of twenty twenty three, and the total passed twenty five million in June of twenty twenty four. The game made the Souls style a mainstream hit.

sections.heading: Shadow of the Erdtree
sections.script: In June of twenty twenty four, Elden Ring got its first huge expansion. Shadow of the Erdtree was released on June twenty first, twenty twenty four, and it sold more than five million units in just three days. Critics loved it. At the time of reporting, it had a Metacritic score of ninety five, the highest for any expansion on the site, while the base game stood at ninety six. Players returned to Elden Ring for a large new area and a fresh set of tough challenges. Some players criticized technical issues and the steep difficulty, and the studio responded with an update, but the overall response was clear. Shadow of the Erdtree was a triumph.

sections.heading: Nightreign and the road ahead
sections.script: FromSoftware did not stop there. Elden Ring Nightreign, announced at The Game Awards two thousand twenty four, launched in late May of twenty twenty five. It is a spin off, not a sequel, and it is designed for groups of three, in a roguelike style where each run is a new expedition. The studio announced that it sold two million copies on its first day and passed three and a half million copies shipped within five days. Meanwhile, Elden Ring Tarnished Edition, which bundles the base game and Shadow of the Erdtree, arrived on Nintendo Switch Two on August twenty eighth, twenty twenty six, after a delay from the original plan. Fans now wait to see what Miyazaki and his team will create next.

sections.heading: Which Souls game is your favorite
sections.script: From a stalled project in two thousand nine to one of the biggest series in gaming, the Souls games have shown that players love a challenge. Demon's Souls, Dark Souls, Bloodborne, Sekiro and Elden Ring all share one thing: the joy of finally beating something that seemed impossible. Now it is your turn. Which FromSoftware game is your favorite, and which boss gave you the hardest time? Do you want a Bloodborne sequel or a new Dark Souls? Tell us in the comments. If you enjoyed this history, like the video and subscribe for more gaming history, and we will see you at the next bonfire. Good luck out there, Tarnished.
